role.title: Senior Backend Engineer
responsibilities: Build and architect core systems for the role
Collaborate with product and cross-functional engineering teams

requirements.text: We are looking for an experienced engineer with 5+ years of Node.js and distributed systems.
Deep expertise in Node.js, TypeScript, and microservices architecture
Experience designing fault-tolerant high-throughput REST and gRPC APIs
Proven leadership in mentoring junior engineers and conducting code reviews
Hands-on experience with Kafka and Redis caching
Knowledge of Kubernetes and CI/CD pipelines

questions.prompt: In a high-concurrency Node.js and TypeScript environment, how do you diagnose event-loop lag, manage memory leaks, and structure asynchronous workflows safely?
questions.answer_outline: Cover event loop phases (timers, poll, check), worker threads for CPU-bound tasks, stream backpressure, heap memory profiling, and TypeScript strict typing practices.

questions.prompt: How do you leverage TypeScript's advanced type system (conditional types, mapped types, template literal types) to build type-safe API clients and data validation layers?
questions.answer_outline: Explain generative utility types, branded primitive types, runtime Zod/TypeBox validation, compile-time exhaustive checks, and eliminating 'any'.

questions.prompt: When designing high-throughput inter-service communication, how do you decide between REST/JSON and gRPC/Protobuf? How do you ensure backward compatibility, rate-limiting, and graceful error handling?
questions.answer_outline: Compare binary Protobuf serialization and HTTP/2 multiplexing with REST simplicity. Address semantic versioning, client SDKs, deadline propagation, and circuit breaking.

questions.prompt: Describe a situation where you had to lead a critical technical decision or mentor an engineer through a complex architectural challenge. How did you handle trade-offs and build team consensus?
questions.answer_outline: Structure with STAR: Highlight initial disagreement, evaluation criteria/RFC, proactive guidance, and measurable positive delivery outcome.

questions.prompt: Describe how you design a production-grade event-driven pipeline using Kafka or similar message streaming systems. How do you handle partition rebalancing, consumer lag, and out-of-order event delivery?
questions.answer_outline: Cover partition keys for ordering guarantees, idempotent consumers, dead-letter queues, backpressure handling, and end-to-end monitoring metrics.

questions.prompt: Walk through how you design automated deployment pipelines and infrastructure as code to guarantee zero-downtime releases and rapid rollback capabilities.
questions.answer_outline: Discuss declarative infrastructure with Terraform, Kubernetes rolling updates vs canary releases, health probes, and automated smoke testing.

questions.prompt: How do your technical strengths, architectural principles, and engineering values align with our product mission and high-velocity shipping culture?
questions.answer_outline: Demonstrate engineering empathy, customer impact focus, ownership mindset, and alignment with modern software engineering practices.

flashcards.front: Node.js Performance: What happens when CPU-intensive computation runs on the main thread?
flashcards.back: The single-threaded event loop blocks, delaying all I/O polling, timers, and active connections. CPU-heavy work must be offloaded to worker threads or external worker queues.

flashcards.front: TypeScript Strictness: How do unknown and any differ in type safety and assignment?
flashcards.back: 'any' turns off all type checking, allowing unsafe property access. 'unknown' requires explicit type narrowing (typeof, instanceof, user-defined type guards) before use.

flashcards.front: API Design: When should you prefer gRPC over REST/JSON in a microservices ecosystem?
flashcards.back: gRPC uses HTTP/2 multiplexing, compact Protobuf binary serialization, and strongly-typed contracts, delivering 5-10x throughput with lower latency for internal inter-service RPCs.

flashcards.front: STAR Behavioural Framework: What are the 4 essential components?
flashcards.back: S (Situation: technical context), T (Task: your objective), A (Action: specific engineering initiatives you took), R (Result: measurable outcome and business impact).

flashcards.front: Caching Strategies: How do you prevent cache stampedes (thundering herd) during key eviction?
flashcards.back: Implement probabilistic early expiration (XFetch algorithm) or use distributed mutex locking so only a single background worker regenerates the cache while others read stale data.

flashcards.front: Production Reliability: What is the difference between liveness and readiness probes?
flashcards.back: Liveness probe checks if the container process is alive (restarts if failed). Readiness probe checks if the pod can accept client traffic (removes from service endpoints if failed).

questions.prompt: Can you walk through your practical engineering experience with Experience in fintech or financial ledger systems? What architectural trade-offs and edge cases did you encounter in production?
questions.answer_outline: Explain core principles, real production application, trade-offs evaluated, and measurable outcomes.

flashcards.front: React Optimization: How does React's Reconciliation differ from DOM mutation?
flashcards.back: React builds and diffs an in-memory Virtual DOM tree using Fiber fibers. Only dirty nodes with changed props or state trigger physical, batched browser DOM updates.

flashcards.front: Databases: When should you choose a columnar database (ClickHouse) over an OLTP RDBMS (PostgreSQL)?
flashcards.back: OLTP RDBMS excels at normalized transactions, row-level ACID updates, and foreign keys. Columnar OLAP excels at high-throughput append-only ingestion and aggregation queries over billions of rows.

flashcards.front: Core Principles: What are the primary production trade-offs of Familiarity with Next.js App Router?
flashcards.back: Balance throughput, operational complexity, testability, failure isolation, and developer maintenance velocity.

flashcards.back: Balance throughput, operational complexity, testability, failure isolation, and developer maintenance velocity.
